clues: Of the plain-bordered ad and the wavy-bordered ad, one ran in the puzzles section and the other in the tides section.
Olive paid exactly 20 dollars less than whoever advertised in the tides section.
Tariq's ad cost exactly 20 dollars more than the one with the dotted border.
Gus did not pick the wavy border.
The ad in the tides section and the $20 ad came from different advertisers: one had a plain border, the other a dotted border.
The ad in the recipes section cost exactly 10 dollars less than Olive's.
hints: Look at Olive's row where advertisers meet prices. Clues 2 and 6 both measure from her. What could she have paid?
Comparisons rule out the ends. Clue 2 keeps Olive off $30 and $40. Clue 6 says someone paid less than she did.
So Olive paid $20. By clue 6 the recipes ad cost $10, and by clue 2 the tides ad cost $40.
Clue 1 puts the wavy border in puzzles or tides, but clue 5 gives the tides ad a plain or dotted border. So wavy ran in puzzles.

solution.key_idea: Clues 2 and 6 pin Olive at $20 from both sides, which puts the recipes ad at $10 and the tides ad at $40.
steps: By clue 2, Olive paid $10 or $20, and the tides ad cost $30 or $40. Clue 6 rules out $10 for Olive.
So Olive paid $20, the recipes ad cost $10 (clue 6), and the tides ad cost $40 (clue 2).
Clue 5 gives the tides ad a plain or dotted border, so by clue 1 the wavy border ran in puzzles, the plain in tides.
The tides ad had the plain border, so by clue 5 the $20 ad had the dotted one. That is Olive's.
By clue 3, Tariq paid $40, so he ran the plain-bordered ad in tides.
At $20 with a dotted border, Olive was not in recipes, tides or puzzles. So she took sports, and the puzzles ad cost $30.
Clue 4 keeps Gus off the wavy $30 puzzles ad, so Lena placed it. Gus paid $10 for a rope border in recipes.
solution.epilogue: Ada sent out corrected invoices: $10 for Gus's rubber boots in recipes, $20 for Olive in sports, $30 for Lena's lamp notice in puzzles, and $40 for Tariq in tides. Nobody paid twice.
